notes: solc 0.7.6. All 18 functions reviewed (permit* and transfer* wrappers forward to Beanstalk/tokens; pipe, etherPipe, readPipe, multiPipe, advancedPipe call the Pipeline contract; farm delegatecalls itself). The only source loop, farm's for over data, is 'while idx < cd[_param1 + 4]' (476), with OZ-style revert-reason bubbling. Implicit loops (25): farm's rotated zero-init of new bytes[](n) ('while idx - 1', P3), 15 memory-to-memory copies left as loops (P7: bytes arguments and results of the pipe calls), ABI encodings of the PipeCall[]/AdvancedPipeCall[] arguments, decodes of bytes[] results and of int96[]/address[] calldata. The Pipeline's own loops are in another contract. No new problem.
summary: A faithful text whose single source loop (farm) is a clear while; the rest of its 26 whiles are the compiler's encoding and copy loops (15 of them unconverted memory copies).
